note: Customer capex firmed on every counterparty since July (TSMC, Micron, Samsung) into a stock down 7.4% in five days on sector beta with upside-paid skew; the first 2027 statement is the line and the broker WFE bar (+38-45%) is the offset, so a modest relief lean on the guidance scale.

Zinc surcharges and the Valmont utility read-through lift Metal Coatings against a Lennox-weak Precoat and a single-source bar that demands +10.8% revenue; near-balanced, capped small because the bar has one source.

JPM's same-day NII raise after the September hike, against a BofA guide set on a one-hike curve and a consensus cut 6.7% in a month, is the one guidance-line item; the JPM expense raise and the faded peer beats keep it modest.

Flows are the line and the ETFGI series puts iShares' August take at about two-thirds of Q2's monthly pace with Vanguard leading, while the Q3 bond rout leaves ending AUM below a $15.67T consensus; sized against an upside-paid skew and four straight up reactions, so a lean, not a call.

Gross margin is the line that drew three straight negative reactions, diesel went to a series record in Q3 after the CFO hoped for H2 relief and supplier pricing re-accelerated, and the stock sits above the average target 2.8% off its high; the record FDI and headcount leverage are real but have not been paid.

GS and JPM printed equities +72% and +49% y/y this morning against an MS equity-line consensus 28% below its own Q2, with IB growing double digits at both peers against a flat MS line, into a stock de-rated to 15x; the same-day fade of the peer beats and July's +0.39% on a record quarter are the counterweight.

A hurricane-free September likely beats on EPS, but this name sold a $1 beat 9.4% in July on decelerating PIF growth, which slowed again every month since; a second hurricane-free Florida year sets up the same excess-profit catch-up that took the stock -5.8% last October, and the +5.4% five-day run-up into a put-bid skew leaves little room.

A $110M microcap up 56% in 20 days on orders that ship in FY2028, with the company's own flat-to-modest FY27 guide implying an H2 below both H1 and last year's H2, no short base to support it, and a history of selling records (-8.5% on a record year); the first call since May is where the H2 trough gets said out loud.

Citi's Securities Services grew fees +4% and NII +7% QoQ this morning against a State Street consensus flat on both lines, after a September fee-guide raise that bought nothing on a tape down 6.8%; the unscheduled $500M severance charge and a 2-of-7 up history keep it small.
